https://www.prokerala.com/news/articles/.text: Sofia, Aug 8 : Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev on Saturday confirmed that an unidentified drone exploded not too far from a Trans-Balkan gas pipeline near the former Kardam border checkpoint close to Romania, local media reported. According to Radev, the drone exploded just one kilometre away from a compressor station of the Trans-Balkan gas pipeline, near the former Kardam border checkpoint, after entering Bulgarian Airspace from Romania, Euronews reported. "Noise made by the drone was detected by Romanian border police, and a loud explosion was subsequently heard by the 'General Toshevo' border police patrol," Radev told reporters. He also noted that both Bulgarian and Romanian authorities had failed to detect the drone as it made its way through the airspaces of two countries. He added that increased surveillance operations will be put in place in the region from now on. To identify the type of drone involved in the explosion, an investigation has been launched into the incident. In July, three drones that entered Romanian airspace without authorisation were shot down in three separate incidents. According to the Ministry of National Defence of Romania, the third drone was shot down 12 km northeast of Sulina, within Romania's territorial waters. According to the investigation conducted by the General Prosecutor's Office, one of the drones shot down is of the Shahed type, used by Russia against Ukraine. After the incident, Romania's Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) declared a member of the Russian Embassy in Bucharest undesirable (persona non grata) and ordered the member to leave the country. The Foreign Ministry also summoned the Ambassador of Russia to its headquarters upon the instructions of Romanian Foreign Minister Oana-Silvia Toiu. During the meeting, the Romanian side expressed its firm protest against these "illegal and irresponsible" actions and emphasised the clear attribution of responsibility. "The summoning came as a firm response to the repeated violations of Romania's airspace between 24 and 26 July 2026, during which the Romanian Armed Forces downed three drones that entered national territory without authorisation. The Russian diplomat was presented with fragments of a drone destroyed on Romanian territory, components which official prosecutor investigations have confirmed to be of Russian origin," the ministry stated on X. –IANS ksk/as Latest News: DMK to expand district units to 110, sets age and tenure limits for office bearers North Korea calls Japan's record defence budget 'war preparation' His development is noticeable every day: Alonso hails Joao Pedro after new Chelsea deal Punnamada lake comes alive as 72nd Nehru Trophy Boat race kicks off Joao Pedro commits long-term future to Chelsea with 2034 deal HM Shah chairs crucial meeting on permanent political solution for Bengal hills Top Stories US court blocks Trump administration from accessing sensitive data of 17 million commercial drivers Trump renews voter ID push before midterms British MPs seek UN intervention to end bloodshed in PoK by Pakistani forces Related Stories What Is Floodlighting in Dating and Why Is Everyone Talking About It? 25 Modern Dating Terms Everyone Should Know in 2026 Parenting Behaviors That May Increase Anxiety in Kids Helping Teens Handle Rejection and Setbacks in Better Ways FAFO Parenting and Child Development: What Parents Need to Know

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text: Israel's Benjamin Netanyahu speaking at the UN. Photograph: Lev Radin/EPA View image in fullscreen Israel's Benjamin Netanyahu speaking at the UN. Photograph: Lev Radin/EPA First Thing newsletter US news First Thing: Netanyahu lambasts Israel’s critics at UN as New York protesters detained More than 100 people arrested, including celebrities, while Israeli PM was claiming war on Gaza is ‘the opposite of genocide’. Plus a Guardian investigation reveals the extents to which some convenience stores fail to honor their prices Martin Belam Fri 25 Sep 2026 06.52 EDT Last modified on Fri 25 Sep 2026 06.54 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Good morning. Israel’s prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, delivered an inflammatory address to the UN in New York, decrying what he said was a global anti-Jewish conspiracy and taking aim at critics of the humanitarian crisis in Gaza. He branded Turkey’s president, Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, a “tyrant”, described Zohran Mamdani as the “antisemitic mayor of New York”, and declared that Israel’s war in Gaza was not a genocide, “it’s the opposite of genocide”. Netanyahu delivered his address just hours after the Palestinian leader Mahmoud Abbas said his delegation was “unlawfully” denied visas by the Trump administration to attend the meeting. Dozens of delegates, inspired by a Palestinian call, walked out of the General Assembly Hall of the UN headquarters as Netanyahu took the stage. What was the reaction on the streets of New York? More than 100 people were arrested outside the UN headquarters as Netanyahu made his address, after a protest drew hundreds of Jewish, Palestinian, Iranian and Lebanese New Yorkers, among others. Susan Sarandon and Hannah Einbinder were among those detained . What has rapper Macklemore announced? The US rapper, removed from Ed Sheeran’s US tour after voicing support of Palestine, has convened a Free Palestine tour to benefit humanitarian aid organisations. The charity show will visit Dublin, Paris and London, with a North American run to be announced. Iran awaiting response from Trump on proposal to open strait of Hormuz in six days View image in fullscreen US aircraft carrier the George Washington launching night air operations. Photograph: Ed Ou/Reuters Iran has said it has told Donald Trump it is willing to open the strait of Hormuz in six days, and to start talks on its nuclear program the day after, so long as the US lifts sanctions on Iran’s oil exports in return, ends the war on all fronts – including in Lebanon – and releases some of Iran’s frozen assets. Privately, Iranian officials believe they could reach a deal with the Americans, but fear Israel will use its influence to pull the US president away from the proposal due to the inclusion of demands over Lebanon. What happened in the Senate about the war? Senate Republicans have blocked a Democratic effort to end the US war with Iran, voting down a House-passed war powers resolution. The measure, which passed the House last week with bipartisan support, failed in the Senate by a 49-50 vote, attracting some Republican support, but not enough to pass. What other developments have there been in the Middle East? Saudi Arabia says it intercepted six ballistic missiles fired by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis, with the latest attacks pushing oil prices ⁠to a one-week high over fears of spiralling supply disruptions. Texas woman triumphs as court upholds acquittal in voting error case View image in fullscreen Crystal Mason had been sentenced to five years in prison in a controversial illegal voting case. Photograph: Desiree Rios/AP The nearly decade-long case of a Black Texas woman who was sentenced to five years in prison in a controversial illegal voting case will end with an acquittal , the state’s highest criminal court has ruled in a 5-4 decision. Crystal Mason has been appealing ever since her 2018 conviction for casting a provisional ballot that ultimately was not counted. What is the latest voting controversy in Nevada? The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) wrongly identified 185 people on Nevada’s voter rolls as non-citizens, state officials said this week, escalating concerns over the shoddy methodology the government is using to raise fear about non-citizen voting ahead of the midterm elections. Why is their backlash against a sheriff in California over voting? The Republican sheriff Chad Bianco must return more than 650,000 ballots his department confiscated earlier this year in an unprecedented move that violated election law, a state supreme court has ruled . At Trump meeting, Xi Jinping lays out terms to avoid US-China military conflict View image in fullscreen Trump and Chinese President Xi at the White House. Photograph: Jim Lo Scalzo/EPA Xi Jinping has called for extensive cooperation with Washington to avoid a trap that could put the US and China on a military collision course amid rising tensions over artificial intelligence, trade and Taiwan. Rather than confrontation, conditions for “achieving the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and making America great again go hand in hand” and should be the goal, Xi said. Mark Saunokonoko has this list of key takeaways from the summit . In other news … View image in fullscreen Mary Peltola. Photograph: Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images Mary Peltola’s campaign says reports of her using slurs and shoving a staffer are exaggerated , but acknowledges the Democratic nominee in Alaska’s pivotal Senate race struggled following the deaths of her husband and mother. Trump’s Food and Drug Administration commissioner nominee, Dr Heidi Overton , has said the MMR vaccine shot is “safe and effective” , weeks after standing behind Trump as he suggested the shot could be “quite lethal”. US mortgage rates surpassed 7% for the first time since January 2025 , according to federal lender Freddie Mac. Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ’s presidential campaign has accused Donald Trump of wanting to “colonise” Brazil in order to capture its natural resources by meddling in next month’s presidential election there. Stat of the day: ICE has wasted tens of millions to carry out Trump’s mass detention agenda View image in fullscreen The Trump administration has spent resources on seeking, detaining and removing people with no criminal history. Photograph: Kevin Mohatt/Reuters US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and other federal agencies have wasted tens of millions of dollars pursuing controversial plans to rapidly increase detention capacity – and the total will likely rise due to continuing mismanagement, congressional investigators have warned . Culture Pick: My dad was a monster! Sara Karloff on reviving Frankenstein, 95 years on View image in fullscreen Michael Shapiro conducting Frankenstein. Photograph: Handout Boris Karloff’s daughter and the composer Michael Shapiro, who has written a 21st-century musical score for the 1931 classic, talk to Pamela Hutchinson about how it became so loved – and the strange experience of watching your father be Dr Frankenstein’s creation as a teenager. Don’t miss this: Gavin Newsom condemns Democrats’ ‘climate hushing’, predicts Trump’s downfall and expects AOC to run in 2028 View image in fullscreen Newsom could yet run for president himself. Photograph: Charly Triballeau/AFP/Getty Images Mark Hertsgaard interviews the governor of California , a man who may still – if the circumstances are right for him – run for US president in 2028. … or this: Amid soaring living costs, America’s biggest convenience-store chains quietly overcharge consumers View image in fullscreen Collage of 7-Eleven and Circle K signs, products and receipts. Illustration: Guardian Design / Getty Images A Guardian investigation has revealed that 7-Eleven and Circle K stores often fail to honor advertised prices – charging more at the pump and register for gas, snacks and other items. Climate check: ‘We wanted to prove we didn’t need air conditioning’ – the airport cooled by natural ventilation View image in fullscreen Roland Garros airport in Réunion. Photograph: Studio Lumière Avoiding a planet-heating disaster will take innovative approaches, and at Roland Garros airport on Réunion island, a unique ceiling design funnels a light tropical breeze into the terminal, ending the need to run air conditioning . Last Thing: 55,000 fans and nowhere to hide – what it’s like to play in basketball’s biggest arena View image in fullscreen Players compete in the Commissioner’s Cup finals in the Philippines. Photograph: Xinhua/Rouelle Umali/Xinhua/Alamy I still have nightmares about just a handful of people watching me flounder at sport in my younger years, so appearing at the sprawling Philippine Arena sounds terrifying. Photograph: Joe Castro/AAP View image in fullscreen Former reality star and wellness influencer Sam Wood will ask the Queensland supreme court to grant him bail as he faces domestic violence charges. Photograph: Joe Castro/AAP Queensland Sam Wood makes bid for bail to supreme court over domestic violence charges Former reality star and wellness influencer stands accused of choking and assaulting wife at Noosa in Queensland Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Ben Smee Queensland state correspondent Wed 21 Oct 2026 21.02 EDT Last modified on Wed 21 Oct 2026 21.55 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Former reality television star Sam Wood will go to the Queensland supreme court seeking release from custody, more than two weeks after he was denied bail over allegations he choked and assaulted his wife. Wood, a 46-year-old wellness influencer from Melbourne, was arrested at Noosa on 4 October on domestic violence allegations. He was refused bail by a Queensland court after police detailed evidence about a similar incident from Victoria about three years ago and argued that his behaviour was “escalating”. Wood is now seeking for the bail decision to be reviewed by the supreme court. Under Queensland’s domestic violence laws, serious charges including “strangulation in a domestic setting” carry a presumption against bail. Wood appeared in a Sunshine Coast court earlier this month charged with two domestic violence offences: assault occasioning bodily harm and strangulation in a domestic setting. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email The court heard that his wife, Snezana, was supportive of the charges and that “there was a cessation of breath” as she was allegedly choked. “She articulates the banging of her head on the floor. She couldn’t breathe,” police prosecutor Jeanette Grigoris said. “She thought she was going to die.” In Wood’s first application for bail, lawyer Matthew Cuskelly said his client denied the allegations. He cited a psychologist’s report that said Sam Wood was suffering from “severe depression”. “He ought to be given the opportunity to engage with mental health professionals,” Cuskelly said. “And also try to salvage something of his professional reputation and career, which is taking a hell of a beating at the moment. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion “Ultimately, as all families have, there was problems. And my client had been enduring the hardship of attempting to quarantine those problems from his family for some period of time. It was agonising.” Cuskelly cited a psychologist’s report that describes “the difficulty that my client has been enduring in respect of the deterioration of his psychological state”. “His depression is regarded as extremely severe.” Wood spent four days in the Maroochydore police watch house after his arrest. He was subsequently held in the high-security Wolston correctional centre near Brisbane. It is understood the supreme court bail hearing won’t take place until next month, meaning Wood will spend at least a month in custody.
